builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: EdgeALM: An Efficient and Unified Edge Accelerator for Large Audio Language Models via Full-Stack Hardware-Software Co-Design and Agent-Driven Recursive Optimization
summary: EdgeALM replaces GPU-based ALM inference with a custom FPGA accelerator combining AWQ-style quantization, modality-conditioned vocabulary pruning, a Conv-Matmul disaggregated architecture, and an extra-coarse-grained ISA, all tuned by agent-driven recursive optimization. It costs the purchase and bring-up of an Alveo U50-class FPGA plus reliance on a bespoke compiler/toolchain and an agent-driven tuning loop, and requires accepting quantization and vocabulary pruning of the target model. It can fail if the compression flow degrades accuracy on the reader's specific audio models, if the custom software stack proves fragile or unmaintained, or if model updates outpace the hardware-specific optimization loop.
rationale: The technique is a full-stack FPGA hardware-software co-design requiring an Alveo U50 and custom ISA/toolchain work, which is outside the reader's GPU/API infrastructure and offers no adoption path on their existing hardware.
technique: FPGA full-stack accelerator for audio LLMs

claims.statement: EdgeALM replaces GPU-based ALM inference with a custom FPGA accelerator combining AWQ-style quantization, modality-conditioned vocabulary pruning, a Conv-Matmul disaggregated architecture, and an extra-coarse-grained ISA, all tuned by agent-driven recursive optimization. It costs the purchase and bring-up of an Alveo U50-class FPGA plus reliance on a bespoke compiler/toolchain and an agent-driven tuning loop, and requires accepting quantization and vocabulary pruning of the target model. It can fail if the compression flow degrades accuracy on the reader's specific audio models, if the custom software stack proves fragile or unmaintained, or if model updates outpace the hardware-specific optimization loop.

Up to 169.5 tokens/s audio-to-text inference for ALMs up to 13B parameters on a single Alveo U50 FPGA (8 GB HBM), with 94% bandwidth utilization, 26 W average power, and real-time streaming audio-to-audio support; higher bandwidth utilization than the EdgeLLM FPGA baseline.
